rationale.compliance: Not a state law but a de-facto market entry condition imposed by GFSI/retailers; drives near-mandatory spend for suppliers.

A traditionally kleinteilig, regionally organised market where consolidators (Eurofins, SGS Institut Fresenius, Merieux/Institut Kirchhoff, Tentamus, AGROLAB) are rolling up a long tail of owner-operated labs.

rationale.recurring: Statutory 'mikrobiologische Eigenkontrollen' are per-batch/per-lot and continuous, driving weekly-to-daily sample flows from every food producer.
rationale.fragmentation: Dozens of regional micro labs (BAV-Institut, Novum Analytik, Selektis, Labor Kneissler, MVZ Ravensburg/Gaertner) coexist with consolidators; low capex per test favours a long owner-operated tail.
rationale.compliance: VO (EG) 2073/2005 sets binding microbiological criteria; testing is mandatory legal spend, not discretionary.

dach_signals.revenue_band_eur: EUR 0.5-5m typical independent; consolidator sites larger

food-agriculture-services-value-chain/an.name: Animal By-Product Disposal & Rendering (Tierkoerperbeseitigung / Kat. 1-3)
food-agriculture-services-value-chain/an.description: Collection, transport, processing and disposal of animal by-products under Reg. (EC) 1069/2009, (EU) 142/2011, TierNebG and TierNebV. Category 1/2 carcass disposal is a public-law duty (Beseitigungspflicht) that Laender/Kreise assign - typically via concession/Beleihung to a designated operator - creating a regional statutory monopoly with no free market-price formation (BVerwG 3 B 61.09); nationwide it is dominated by SecAnim (Saria/Rethmann group). Category 3 material (former foodstuffs, slaughter by-products) feeds rendering, petfood, oleochemical and biodiesel value chains with more open private competition (Saria/ReFood and others). Investability is therefore restricted overall: the Cat 1/2 tendered public-law monopoly is effectively closed to financial investors, while Cat 3 processing is open.

rationale.fragmentation: Cat 1/2 disposal is regionally monopolistic (assigned concessions), so overall fragmentation is low despite a more open Cat 3 tier.
rationale.compliance: Fully governed by EU animal-by-product law plus TierNebG/TierNebV; disposal is legally mandatory.

dach_signals.est_players: Cat 1/2: regional monopoly concessions (SecAnim dominant, ~180 collection vehicles nationwide, plus public Zweckverbaende/TBA); Cat 3: rendering/petfood/oleochemical/biodiesel processors

food-agriculture-services-value-chain/ag.name: Herd-health / large-animal veterinary services (Bestandsbetreuung)
food-agriculture-services-value-chain/ag.description: Mobile large-animal veterinary practices (Tierarzt-Fahrpraxis) providing recurring on-farm herd-health management (Bestandsbetreuung), integrated veterinary care and antibiotic/Tierarzneimittel (TAM) usage monitoring for dairy, pig and poultry units. Recurring, compliance-linked on-farm spend tied to antibiotics/TAM documentation duties. Practice ownership is professionally reserved: under the tieraerztliche Berufsordnung the majority of shares and voting rights must be held by, and the practice managed by, licensed veterinarians - so outside/financial ownership is barred, making the segment investability-blocked despite attractive recurring economics.

rationale.compliance: Prescribing and TAM/antibiotics monitoring are legally reserved veterinary acts under TAMG plus the Berufsordnung.
rationale.recurring: Bestandsbetreuung is delivered under standing herd-health/integrated-care contracts with regular on-farm visits.
rationale.fragmentation: Owner-run large-animal/mixed practices spread across rural DACH; no national consolidator.
rationale.scale: Individual Fahrpraxen are small (single-digit-vet), limiting standalone scale.
rationale.margin: Solid owner economics but labour-bound (vet time), capping margin.
rationale.growth: Structurally flat-to-declining livestock numbers temper volume growth.
rationale.headroom: Professional-ownership reservation blocks buy-and-build, so investor headroom is low.
rationale.reimbursement_risk: Fees are paid by farmers (no state reimbursement), but antibiotic-reduction policy can compress TAM-linked volume - low-moderate.
